new_topics.label: Delegated authority and action budgets
new_topics.definition: Which actions a worker may take, who may authorize them, and which time, attempt or resource limit ends the delegation.

new_topics.label: Compatibility, replay and decision history
new_topics.definition: How a stored decision keeps its original meaning across retries, migrations and policy changes, and when a new decision is appropriate.

new_topics.label: Operational diagnosis and recovery
new_topics.definition: How engineers identify the state an application actually used, distinguish competing causes and restore service while preserving incident evidence.

new_topics.label: Concurrency and idempotency
new_topics.definition: How transaction boundaries, request identity and repeated or concurrent operations affect durable state and observable results.

new_topics.label: Expect, Delegate, Observe, Decide (EDOD)
new_topics.definition: ESA’s work order records the expected behavior, the authority delegated to the agent, the observations of the identified candidate and the engineer’s decision about what to accept or do next. Appendix C collects the four steps on a field card (7 × 10 print source, p. 293).

books.title: Loop Engineering for AI Agents
books.subtitle: Design Reliable Agentic AI Systems Beyond the Prompt
books.author: Enrico Papalini
books.scope: Chapter titles, section references and starts from the author's final Packt print interior (Contents pp. v–x, Preface pp. xii–xiii); titles cross-checked against the published table of contents. Page numbers are the supplied print interior's printed folios. Retail ISBNs refer to the published edition.
books.summary: An engineering guide to designing a bounded agent loop, protecting its verification, and measuring the cost of the outcome it accepts.
books.source: Author-supplied final Packt print interior, Contents pp. v–x and Preface pp. xii–xiii.
books.cover_provenance: Author companion repository, imgs/cover.jpg. Matched against the print ISBN cover.

chapters.title: Loop Engineering for AI Agents: A Critical Assessment
chapters.summary: The chapter traces the transition from prompting to a persistent loop, with a worker that proposes changes and an independent evaluator that decides when to accept them.

topics.rationale: Following work across multiple attempts changes the completion contract.
A worker proposes a result and a separate evaluator judges it.
Progress must survive a change of context.
Delegation levels assign different decisions to the worker and its supervisor.

related_reading.rationale: The NDSE2 chapter sets out agent capability limits that the loop then has to detect.

external_reading.rationale: Compares the outcome sought by a human with the nested loops used to build software.

practice.rationale: Separate proposal and acceptance when testing a completion contract.

chapters.title: The Organization Becomes a Loop
chapters.summary: The chapter assigns ownership, verification and escalation responsibilities to teams, compares three operating models and examines what changes when governance moves into the runtime.

topics.rationale: Operating models distribute responsibility for accepting and escalating work.
Runtime governance makes decision rights enforceable.
The operating models describe how people and agents share work.
An escalation transfers a decision that exceeds the worker’s remit.

related_reading.rationale: Compare runtime governance with the division of responsibility inside the engineering team.

external_reading.rationale: Review and integration capacity constrain how many parallel tasks one person can supervise.

practice.rationale: Assign ownership of shared targets before coordinating multiple workers.

chapters.title: The Economics of Loop Engineering
chapters.summary: The chapter costs an accepted outcome, including review and retries, and uses a regulated maintenance example to compare local speed with delivery throughput.

topics.rationale: Review, retries and verification all contribute to the cost of an accepted result.
Generating changes faster can leave end-to-end throughput unchanged.
The regulated maintenance example follows work waiting for review.

related_reading.rationale: Both chapters examine adoption costs and the outcome the organization pays for.

external_reading.rationale: The measurement interviews connect adoption to delivery, quality and developer experience.

practice.rationale: Price the next attempt together with the work needed to verify it.

chapters.title: The Ralph Loop: Persistent Progress Through Fresh Context
chapters.summary: The chapter follows one work item through a fresh context, an external plan, a verifier and a checkpoint. It compares shell, stop-hook and editor-driven variants and describes when to escalate.

topics.rationale: A persistent plan and checkpoints carry useful state into a fresh session.
The Ralph pattern gives each attempt a fresh context and one work item.
Failure and repeated attempts trigger escalation or a stop.

related_reading.rationale: A new session relies on state retained outside the model’s context.

external_reading.rationale: Compare the fresh-context pattern with guidance for agents working across sessions.

practice.rationale: Compare the external shell loop with the other Ralph variants.

chapters.title: Building a Full Local AI Loop
chapters.summary: A local reference implementation connects the model runtime, durable plan, protected verifier, retry and recovery policy, observability and human authority.

topics.rationale: The reference design separates runtime, durable plan and verifier.
The worker cannot decide whether its own change satisfies a protected check.
Retry, recovery and human escalation are explicit loop decisions.
A local runtime still needs limits on tools and attempts.
The reference loop records failures and supports resuming from a checkpoint.

related_reading.rationale: A local runtime introduces security boundaries around tools and workspaces.

external_reading.rationale: The harness article covers durable state, checks, recovery and the execution environment.

practice.rationale: Distinguish a successful check from permission to take an action.

chapters.title: Choosing the Right Loop
chapters.summary: The chapter matches an observed failure to the smallest suitable mechanism and tests the selection framework on a customer-support case involving retrieval, checks, budgets and escalation.

topics.rationale: An observed failure determines which loop mechanism to add.
External checks distinguish evidence of progress from a worker’s claim.
The choice of mechanism depends on what another attempt costs.
The customer-support case bounds actions and defines when a human takes over.

related_reading.rationale: Both chapters ask which intervention fits the engineering problem at hand.

external_reading.rationale: Repeated edits to already-clean code provide a bounded example for discussing an explicit stopping condition.

practice.rationale: Define the signal that sends an unresolved decision to a human.

intellectual_lineage.rationale: The author identifies the agentic foundations of Non-Deterministic Autonomous Coding Agents as a starting point for this book.
The author credits the engineering principles of Non-Deterministic Software Engineering. The copyright page gives no edition or ISBN.

books.lineage_locator: Author-supplied Packt interior, copyright page (unnumbered), paragraph above the ISBN and disclaimer.

books.title: Engineering Software with Agentic AI
books.subtitle: Reliable Change with Coding Agents
books.author: Enrico Papalini
books.summary: A practical handbook in which engineers define an outcome, delegate a bounded change to a coding agent, observe the work and decide what can be accepted. A reservation service and a Treasury router carry those decisions into implementation, verification, release and recovery.
books.scope: 5.6.1 identifies the source manuscript. The author's final KDP metadata names this as first commercial edition. The ASIN and Amazon URL were supplied by the author.
books.print_locator_note: Printed page numbers in the 7 × 10 English edition; TOC on pp. iii–iv.

chapters.title: The first accountable change
chapters.summary: Tie a Treasury repair to the approved business rule, the candidate under review and the evidence for accepting, rejecting or escalating it.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 2, chapter 1. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch006.xhtml#chapter-1

topics.rationale: The approved Treasury rule determines the expected result before the repair.
The engineer derives the expected boundary behavior before inspecting the candidate.
The work order identifies who may accept, stop or escalate the repair.
The Treasury repair introduces the four decisions and transfers them to the reservation case.

related_reading.rationale: Compare how the two books define an accountable change and the decision to accept it.

external_reading.rationale: The outcome loop clarifies who owns the result of a delegated change.

practice.rationale: A separate decision-maker checks whether the candidate meets the approved rule.

chapters.title: From need to a verifiable outcome
chapters.summary: Investigate a request for a reservation service. Separate assumptions and observable problems, compare interventions, and choose an outcome whose success can be measured.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 16, chapter 2. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch007.xhtml#chapter-2

topics.rationale: The reservation request is reframed as a verifiable outcome.
The chapter compares possible interventions and defines a measure before implementation.
Unresolved claims shape the contract for the next step.

related_reading.rationale: A verifiable outcome becomes an intention that can be carried into a change contract.

external_reading.rationale: Compare the resulting work order with advice on writing a compact, testable agent specification.

practice.rationale: Investigate an unresolved assumption before committing to a plan.

chapters.title: Specify behavior and acceptance
chapters.summary: Use boundary examples, refusals and event sequences to distinguish interpretations of a reservation contract. Turn unresolved questions into decisions for the owner.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 29, chapter 3. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch008.xhtml#chapter-3

topics.rationale: Boundary examples, refusals and event sequences make competing interpretations visible.
Acceptance examples let another engineer challenge the implementation.

related_reading.rationale: Compare boundary examples with the NDSE2 treatment of intention contracts.

external_reading.rationale: The survey compares how specification workflows express intent before implementation.

practice.rationale: An approved behavioral specification supplies the starting point for the implementation.

chapters.title: Context, memory, tools and agent boundaries
chapters.summary: Identify which instructions, permissions and tools a worker actually has. Promote verified claims into memory and revoke or revise them when their source changes.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 43, chapter 4. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch010.xhtml#chapter-4

topics.rationale: Claims enter memory only with a source and criteria for later revision.
Loaded instructions, tool permissions and enforced boundaries determine what a worker can do.
A checked handoff records what the next session can rely on.

related_reading.rationale: Fresh-context loops depend on the same distinction between durable claims and transient session state.

external_reading.rationale: Rules, subagents, hooks and external context illustrate different ways information reaches an agent.

practice.rationale: Store a checked claim together with its provenance for a later session.

chapters.title: Design and prototype alternatives
chapters.summary: Compare two designs under the same approved behavior, prototype their riskiest assumption and record the conditions for revisiting the design decision.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 59, chapter 5. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch011.xhtml#chapter-5

topics.rationale: Two candidate designs are compared under the same behavioral invariants.
A prototype tests the riskiest assumption before a design is retained.
A decision record preserves the reasons and conditions for revisiting the design.

related_reading.rationale: Compare the prototype decision with the architectural constraints used to judge a retained change.

external_reading.rationale: A compiling candidate can still distort a type model or add unnecessary mechanisms.

practice.rationale: Prototype alternatives under the same contract before deciding which one to retain.

chapters.title: Plan, delegate and orchestrate
chapters.summary: Split work by dependencies and handoffs. Budget attempts, use observations to guide retries and test the integrated result across workers.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 72, chapter 6. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch012.xhtml#chapter-6

topics.rationale: Work is split into handoffs with named ownership across workers.
A budget and a stopping condition constrain the next attempt.
Feedback distinguishes a useful refusal from a retry or escalation.
The work order sets the expected result, bounds an attempt and records the observation and verdict before another attempt is authorized.

related_reading.rationale: Team boundaries and handoffs determine who can accept integrated work.

external_reading.rationale: Parallel coding accounts contrast simultaneous execution with serial review and integration.

practice.rationale: Make dependencies and integration checks explicit before work is divided.

chapters.title: Implement and debug a bounded change
chapters.summary: Trace a failing value through a bounded change, distinguish fixture and product failures and preserve the candidate for independent review.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 88, chapter 7. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch014.xhtml#chapter-7

topics.rationale: Tracing a value reveals the boundary where its meaning changes.
The bounded candidate is retained for a separate engineering judgment.
A diagnostic trace distinguishes a fixture failure from a product failure before acting.
The engineer traces an observed failure, delegates a bounded repair and hands over an identified candidate for decision.

related_reading.rationale: Understanding an existing system helps locate the first point where an observed value changes meaning.

external_reading.rationale: Brownfield guidance pairs recovery of tacit constraints with regression evidence.

practice.rationale: Keep the repair small enough for its behavior to be traced and checked.

chapters.title: Verify the contract independently
chapters.summary: Derive expected results independently. Challenge apparently passing checks with properties and controlled faults, and test the actual consumer as well as its provider.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 103, chapter 8. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch015.xhtml#chapter-8

topics.rationale: Independent expected values and controlled faults test whether a passing check can detect a bad change.
Section 8.8 verifies state transitions under concurrency at their actual boundary.
Surviving faults reveal what a set of tests can distinguish.

related_reading.rationale: Compare the chapter’s four dimensions of independence with the loop’s separation of worker and evaluator.

external_reading.rationale: The exploratory TDD comparison shows why tests written inside the same loop deserve additional scrutiny.

practice.rationale: Challenge an apparently passing check with a deterministic failure case.

chapters.title: Review, integrate and release with evidence
chapters.summary: Bind review claims to the integrated candidate and extracted release artifact. Record who can accept, release or restore it, and recheck assumptions at the point of action.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 120, chapter 9. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch016.xhtml#chapter-9

topics.rationale: Review evidence is bound to the integrated and packaged artifact.
Readiness, acceptance and authority to release are distinct decisions.
The rollback contract identifies the object and conditions for restoring service.
The work order follows the identified candidate through integration and packaging to the decision to accept, release or restore it.

related_reading.rationale: Compare release authority for one candidate with runtime governance across teams.

external_reading.rationale: The review essay discusses the effort required to justify accepting an AI-generated change.

practice.rationale: Keep verification evidence attached to the identity of the packaged candidate.

chapters.title: Evolve with compatible history
chapters.summary: Separate replay from reassessment as policies change. Preserve transaction identity, history and compatibility across schema migrations and external effects.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 136, chapter 10. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch018.xhtml#chapter-10

topics.rationale: A replay uses the recorded decision, while reassessment applies a new policy.
Request identity and a transaction boundary control duplicate effects.
Reader/writer compatibility affects the order in which storage formats can change.

related_reading.rationale: Compatibility obligations constrain the design of the next change to persistent state.

external_reading.rationale: The migration case offers a comparison for checking behavior while replacing an existing representation.

practice.rationale: Keep a regression check for the meaning of previously recorded decisions.

chapters.title: Diagnose the system that actually ran
chapters.summary: Distinguish candidate causes of an incident by observing the configuration, policy and ledger actually in use. Retain evidence while restoring service.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 150, chapter 11. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch019.xhtml#chapter-11

topics.rationale: Read-only observations distinguish the active configuration and ledger before recovery.
Restoring service preserves the separate histories of the states being examined.
Competing causal explanations predict different observations of the running system.

related_reading.rationale: Reconstructing a running system requires evidence of the configuration and state it actually selected.

external_reading.rationale: Diagnostics can expose which observation an engineer or agent needs to distinguish failure modes.

practice.rationale: Require a causal explanation grounded in observations before retaining the repair.

chapters.title: Learning, adoption and the whole cost
chapters.summary: Evaluate a bounded adoption trial with reviewer effort, quality, cost per accepted outcome and evidence of what maintainers can retain and transfer.
chapters.source_locator: English 7 × 10 print source, p. 161, chapter 12. EPUB: EPUB/text/ch020.xhtml#chapter-12

topics.rationale: Whole-cost accounting includes review, retries and the cost of an accepted result.
Retention and transfer are checked separately from task completion.
A bounded adoption trial tests sensitivity to cost and quality assumptions.
The book asks what judgment remains available to maintainers after delegation.

related_reading.rationale: Compare the adoption trial’s cost per accepted result with Packt’s economics of an engineering loop.

external_reading.rationale: Company measurement examples provide a comparison for the trial’s baseline and its delivery and quality measures.

practice.rationale: Measure the accepted outcome and the effort required to obtain it.
